residue.text: Registration independently enables receipt requests. Bulk adds queued work without adding validation or server capacity. Both arms predict eight registrations; recognition failure remains independently visible. Extra capacity, repair, and alternate channels are unavailable.

N8 can succeed only at ticks 6 through 8. Control predicts its delivery at tick 8; increased bulk loses that slot. These are finite-model predictions, not observed executions or global schedule optimality.

Exceptional display-delay origin, empirical network distribution, and later sender adaptation remain unknown. No new demand occurs here; hypothetical later status traffic cannot establish present harm.

summary.text: Proposed control: validate N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5. Request individual N2,N3,N4,N5 at ticks 0,1,2,3; bulk at 5; individual N8 at 6. Predicted deliveries: N2,N3,N4,N5 at 1,2,3,4; idle at 5; N6,N7,N8 at 6,7,8. Initial N1 recognition yields eight recognitions; registrations reach eight.

Increase preferred intervention by replacing only tick-0 individual with bulk: two bulk requests instead of one, still six actions. Predicted N1 duplicate at tick 1 shifts N5 delivery to tick 5. Unchanged tick-5 bulk captures pending N5 before that delivery; its duplicate consumes tick 6. N6,N7 deliver at 7,8; N8 remains queued beyond the window. Recognition falls to seven.

Predeclare harm detector: at least two nonprogress server slots among ticks 1 through 8, counting duplicate, failure, or idle. Eight slots must supply seven new recognitions; two nonprogress slots force failure. Control predicts one idle; increased bulk predicts two duplicates. Threshold precedes results.

Closest rival hypothesis: batching benefit preserves eight recognitions despite stale display. FIFO-interference hypothesis instead predicts increased-bulk duplicates at ticks 1 and 6 and seven recognitions versus control eight.

Feasible separating probe: replay both schedules from identical stipulated starting states, changing only tick-0 request type. Compare registrations, pending identities, FIFO entries, first deliveries, and boundary-9 recognition. Defeat: increased bulk reaches eight recognitions or lacks predicted duplicates. Per arm: six validation ticks, six dispatcher actions; ledger reads add no clerk labor. Execution remains unobserved.
